evals.prompt: I'm in Plan Mode on Claude Opus 4.7 drafting a plan for a small CRUD API. I don't want to pay Opus rates for the actual implementation — I'd rather have a cheaper model like Composer do the file edits. How do I set that up in this project (which doesn't have anything installed yet)?
evals.expected_output: The agent detects first-use (no marker file exists), explains the 7-question setup interview, and conducts the interview via AskQuestion before generating any files. After the interview it invokes scripts/setup.py with the answers as JSON, reports the generated files, and explains the per-plan tier-selection flow plus the /orchestrate command.
expectations: The skill detects first-use by checking for the marker file `.cursor-orchestrator-installed` at both project and user-wide scopes.
The agent announces that first-use setup is required before generating any files.
The agent runs the 7-question setup interview using AskQuestion (scope, tiers, default tier, verifier, rule, commands, max_mode).
After the interview, the agent invokes `python scripts/setup.py --answers <json>` with a valid answers payload.
The agent explains the per-plan tier question that will be asked before finalizing plans.
The agent surfaces the Build-button caveat — native Build runs on the picker model; /orchestrate is what dispatches to the configured tier.
The agent does NOT write agent/rule files directly — it delegates to setup.py so the SHA-hash-tracked marker is created.

evals.prompt: I just saved this plan to .cursor/plans/widget-crud.plan.md after using the cursor-orchestrator skill to add an execution block (implementation_model: composer, parallelism: sequential, verify_each_step: true). It has 4 todos: schema migration, API endpoints, creation form, and integration tests. Execute it.
evals.expected_output: The agent recognizes this as an orchestration task, invokes the /orchestrate (or /plan-orchestrator) sub-agent with the plan path, and explains that each todo will be dispatched to /impl-composer with a verifier pass between steps. The agent does not make code edits directly — it coordinates.
expectations: The agent invokes /orchestrate with the plan path or delegates to /plan-orchestrator directly (does not try to implement steps itself).
The agent correctly identifies that the tier is `composer` → dispatches to `/impl-composer` sub-agent (not /impl-fast, /impl-mini, etc.).
The agent respects `verify_each_step: true` by planning to invoke /verifier between steps.
The agent updates each todo's `status` in the plan file as execution progresses (pending → in_progress → completed).
The agent produces a final summary report of what was implemented, what was verified, and any failures.
The agent does NOT make file edits itself during the orchestration phase.

evals.prompt: Cursor just announced Composer 3 with better pricing. I want my orchestrator to start using it. Can you refresh the model catalog and update my sub-agent files? I've also hand-edited `.cursor/agents/impl-composer.md` to add a custom instruction — please don't overwrite that.
evals.expected_output: The agent invokes the /update-orchestrator command, which runs scripts/update_models.py to fetch the latest pricing page, diffs against the cached catalog, asks for confirmation before regenerating, and then calls scripts/generate_agents.py --regenerate. The user-edited impl-composer.md is preserved (SHA mismatch → skipped with a warning).
expectations: The agent invokes /update-orchestrator (or runs the underlying scripts/update_models.py + generate_agents.py --regenerate sequence).
The agent runs update_models.py first to fetch and diff the catalog before regenerating anything.
The agent shows the user the catalog diff (added/removed/repriced/retiered models) before asking for confirmation.
The agent asks for confirmation before regenerating sub-agent files.
The user-edited `impl-composer.md` is NOT overwritten — the SHA mismatch protection correctly identifies it as user-modified and skips it with a warning in the report.
The agent reports which files were regenerated, which were skipped, and the new tier mapping.
